label: TP
reason: Alert 1 (java/xss): alert-TP — User input flows through Base64 encode/decode (preserves payload) to bar, which is concatenated into SQL string at line 52, then sql is passed to encodeForHTML() at lines 62-63 in the exception handler. While encodeForHTML() applies HTML encoding, the vulnerable path is the SQL injection at line 52 where bar is directly concatenated into the SQL query without parameterization. Alert 2 (java/sql-injection): alert-TP — User input flows through param → doSomething() → bar → sql string concatenation at line 52. Bar contains unescaped user input that is directly inserted into the SQL query. Both alerts represent real vulnerabilities: SQL injection allows attackers to manipulate the WHERE clause via crafted input.

evidence.note: doSomething() passes param through Base64 encode/decode cycle, preserving user input in bar
SQL query constructed by concatenating bar directly into SQL string without parameterization
XSS sink: encodeForHTML(sql) called in exception handler, but SQL injection vulnerability exists upstream at line 52
